CONFIRM C0050 — FIND: `EvidenceRecord.from_chain_record()` sets `er.experiment = meta.get("experiment", "")`, but `EvidenceStore.from_chain_file()` derives the store’s experiment name from the directory. In PoC logs, metadata often omits `experiment`, so `_EvidenceIndex.by_experiment` stays empty and `query(experiment=...)` returns no records even though the store has a valid experiment context. Evidence: in `evidence.py`, constructor passes `experiment_name` only to `self._experiment`; it is never propagated into records/indexing. This is a real partitioning bug for one of the module’s advertised query dimensions.

CHALLENGE C0046 | `trace_finding()` currently iterates `for i in sorted(indices)` and emits `rec.timestamp_utc` verbatim. Record index order is chain append order, not guaranteed chronological order by timestamp. But this exact issue is already closed as C0024/C0003/C0007. The open statement for C0046 appears to duplicate resolved chronology defects unless it contains new, distinct evidence beyond “unsorted event list,” which the current code does not have by index. As stated, it is not a new confirmed bug.

CHALLENGE C0016 | The proposed fix does not match the actual code path. `verify_bundle()` verifies each embedded proof with `self._chain.verify_inclusion_proof(proof, bundle.merkle_root)`, and `VerificationChain.verify_inclusion_proof()` is stateless with respect to chain contents; it only checks the supplied proof against the supplied root. Evidence from `verification_chain.py`: it reads `proof["chain_hash"]`, `proof["proof"]`, and `merkle_root`, with no access to `self._records`/`self._epochs`. Adding a standalone wrapper is unnecessary for correctness. The real bundle-verification defects in this area were already closed under C0009/C0034/C0039.

DESCRIPTION: FIND — `bench/evidence.py`, `EvidenceStore.export_bundle()`, lines around the filter path. When exporting by `finding_id`, `model`, or `round_idx`, the method calls `_index.search(...)` without restricting by experiment, even though the module advertises entity-indexed queries and bundles “for this experiment.” If a chain file contains records whose metadata names a different experiment, `export_bundle()` can silently mix records across experiments into one bundle. Evidence: `export_bundle()` computes `indices = self._index.search(finding_id=..., model=..., round_idx=...)`; unlike a direct `query(experiment=...)`, no experiment filter is applied. `_EvidenceIndex` explicitly supports `by_experiment`, so this omission is observable in code.
FOLLOW: The same cross-experiment contamination affects all non-index-based bundle exports, including reviewer workflows like `export_bundle(finding_id="C0042")` and `export_bundle(model="Gemini", round_idx=5)`. The resulting `EvidenceBundle.experiment` field is set to `self._experiment`, so the bundle can be mislabeled as belonging to one experiment while containing records from another. `verify_bundle()` will still report the bundle valid because inclusion proofs are cryptographic, so this becomes a silent semantic integrity failure rather than a cryptographic one.

DESCRIPTION: FIND — `bench/evidence.py`, `EvidenceStore.summary()`, lines around `merkle_root = epochs[-1]["merkle_root"] if epochs else ""`. For an unsealed but non-empty chain, `summary()` reports an empty Merkle root even though `export_bundle()` for the same store computes a valid root from current records. Evidence from code: `summary()` uses epoch root only; `export_bundle()` has explicit fallback `rfc9162_merkle_root(leaves)` when `epochs` is empty. This makes the advertised “Store summary — record counts by type, model, round” semantically inconsistent with bundle export and misrepresents current chain state.
FOLLOW: Any UI/CLI using `summary().merkle_root` to display the current audit anchor will show blank on fresh PoC chains before the first seal, while bundle export and proof generation can already operate. That can mislead the human reviewer into thinking no root exists or the chain is unusable. The inconsistency is especially visible when comparing `summary()` output immediately before `export_bundle()`.

DESCRIPTION: FIND — `bench/evidence.py`, `EvidenceStore.verify_bundle()`. The method iterates with `zip(bundle.records, bundle.inclusion_proofs)` and returns success if no collected errors exist. If a malformed bundle has fewer proofs than records, extra records are silently skipped and the function can return `(True, [])`. Evidence: Python `zip()` truncates to the shorter iterable; there is no precondition check that lengths match. The function contract says “verify all inclusion proofs in a bundle,” so silent truncation violates that contract.
FOLLOW: This permits incomplete bundles to pass verification while omitting proof checks for tail records. Because `export_bundle()` itself emits matching lengths, the bug primarily affects external or tampered bundles — exactly the verification scenario this API exists for. The false positive propagates to any audit tool relying on `verify_bundle()` as a complete bundle validator.
